plain: Coming from outside a thing; not part of its nature.

webster.text: External; outward; not contained in or belonging to a body.

example.quote: If, then, a power to erect a corporation in any case be deducible, by fair inference, from the whole or any part of the numerous provisions of the Constitution of the United States arguments drawn from extrinsic circumstances regarding the in tension of the Convention must be rejected.
example.cite: Alexander Hamilton, Opinion as to the Constitutionality of the Bank of the United States, Feb. 23, 1791
